text: Working ticket #1720 (bundle the bridge extension in the package). Reading the call sites next.
Now the code: the build script first.
Move the copy after the stale-browser stop, so a leftover browser isn't watching files being rewritten.
Those daemon failures are the known "no `dist/` in a fresh worktree" case. Building, then testing again.
Node tests all pass (1236). The dashboard's vitest run shows 535 failures, so I'm checking whether that comes from my change.
Now the LOGIC.md files and the README.
Now the ticket's `PR:` line, then I release the claim.

I took the only ticket in the queue, #1720: ship the bridge extension inside the framework package, so the bridge browser works from `npx the-framework`. The work is in PR [#1789](https://github.com/framework/the-framework/pull/1789), set to merge on its own once its checks pass. I haven't launched the bridge browser from an installed package, so the npx path is untested end to end.

**What changed**
- **Build:** a new script, `scripts/copy-extension.mjs`, copies the extension into `dist/chrome-extension` after the compile step. It copies exactly the files the extension's self-reload watches, read from the extension's own list, so the copy can't miss a file and silently turn the self-reload off.
- **Launch (`src/bridge-browser.ts`):**
  - It uses the checkout's `packages/chrome-extension` first, then the package's copy. A folder only counts if its manifest names the bridge extension.
  - A checkout still installs from where it is, so edits there still reach the running browser without a rebuild.
  - A package's copy is first copied into the bridge browser's own `extension` folder and installed from there. Chrome bases the extension's id on its folder, and npx puts each version in a new folder, so without this the browser profile would collect a dead extension copy for every version.
- **Tests:** new tests cover which folder is picked, skipping a folder whose manifest names another extension, the build's copy against the watched-files list, and installing from the bridge browser's folder.
- **Docs:** I updated the LOGIC.md files, added one for the new script, and updated the extension README.

**Checks**
- The package's node test suite passes (1236 tests), and the typecheck passes.
- `npm pack --dry-run` lists the seven files under `dist/chrome-extension`.
- The dashboard test run fails in this worktree: 535 tests fail with React errors (hooks read as null), which usually means two copies of React are loaded. This change touches no dashboard code, but I didn't run those tests on `main` to confirm they fail there too. The PR description says the same.

**Queue and ticket:** the queue entry is marked done, and the ticket now has the line `PR: [#1789](…)`, so it counts as in review. I released my claim. The PR description has `Closes tickets/2026-08-26_ship-bridge-extension-in-package.md` and `Closes #1720`, so the ticket closes when the PR merges. My branch is `agent-ship-bridge-extension`.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need to be authorized in your claude.ai connector settings; I didn't need them here, and they can't be used until then.
